Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE in color_string_to_rgba() (libavcodec/xpmdec.c) during XPM image decoding. The function declares a fixed 100-byte stack buffer `char color_name[100]` and copies a caller-supplied color token of length `len` into it. Before the fix, `len` was neither lower-bounded (it could be negative, wrapping to huge when used as a size) nor upper-bounded against sizeof(color_name)-1. A crafted XPM file with an oversized or malformed color name string causes the copy to write past the end of the stack buffer. Fix adds `len = FFMIN(FFMAX(len, 0), sizeof(color_name) - 1)` before any access.

Index-out-of-bounds (UBSAN) in getRegisterName() -> printMemOperand() -> printInstruction() in Capstone's ARM disassembler. When disassembling the `tbh [r0, r1, lsl #1]` instruction, printAddrModeTBH() fills in mem.base and mem.index on the current operand slot but omits setting shift.type and shift.value. A subsequent code path reads these uninitialized fields to compute an array index into the register name table, producing an out-of-bounds access. Fix adds the two missing assignments `shift.type = ARM_SFT_LSL; shift.value = 1` alongside the existing mem.lshift assignment.

Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 in ares_parse_aaaa_reply() when the caller supplies a TTL output array (addrttls) with fewer slots than the number of AAAA records in the DNS response. The function parses all AAAA records from the wire-format response, counting them into naddrs, then iterates up to naddrs writing TTL values into the caller's addrttls[] array without checking against *naddrttls (the caller-declared capacity). If the DNS response contains more records than the caller allocated slots for, the loop writes past the end of the caller's stack buffer. The same bug exists in ares_parse_a_reply().

SEGV (wild address read) in decUnitCompare() (decNumber.c) during decimal number comparison. Reached via decCompare -> decCompareOp -> decNumberCompare -> jvp_number_cmp -> jv_cmp, invoked from constant_fold()/gen_binop() in the jq parser (parser.y) while constant-folding a binary comparison expression at compile time, indicating a thread-local decContext or decNumber value is invalid/uninitialized when the parser folds a comparison during jq_compile.

Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 in decToString()/decNumberToString() reached via jv_number_get_literal() when stringifying a jq number with a very large negative exponent. jv_number_get_literal() allocates a buffer of size (digits + 14) to hold the decimal string representation, following the decNumber library's documented requirement. However decNumberToString() writes a NUL terminator after the last character of the output, requiring a buffer of (digits + 14 + 1). For numbers like -10E-1000010001 (which normalises to -1.0E-1000010000, with 'digits' computed from the exponent magnitude), the NUL byte lands exactly one byte past the end of the heap allocation.

Heap-buffer-overflow READ in pcre2_fuzzsupport.c. The fuzz harness pre-scans the pattern for quantifier sequences like ')digits{' so it can clamp oversized quantifiers before calling pcre2_compile(). The scan loop `for (size_t i = 1; i < size - 2; i++)` computes `size - 2` on an unsigned size_t; for inputs shorter than 3 bytes this underflows to a near-SIZE_MAX value instead of the loop being skipped, so the scan reads far past the end of the heap-allocated input buffer.

Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE in xmlSnprintfElementContent() (valid.c) while formatting an XML element content model description for error reporting. The function writes a human-readable representation of a DTD element declaration into a fixed-size caller-supplied stack buffer, recursively processing child nodes. Two separate buffer-space checks failed to account for the length of separators and element name strings correctly: one omitted the length of the '|' separator, and another did not correctly check remaining space before appending an element name. A DOCTYPE with a deeply nested or unusually long element name overflows the stack buffer. Fixes CVE-2017-9047 and CVE-2017-9048.

Index-out-of-bounds (UBSAN) in add_ff_action() -> dissect_data_encap() in Wireshark's IEEE 802.11 dissector (packet-ieee80211.c). The dissector maps HE (802.11ax High Efficiency) channel feedback frames to arrays of scidx (subcarrier index) start/end pairs, e.g. scidx_20MHz_Ng4[9]. An attacker-controlled field in the HE Compressed Beamforming Report selects which group-of-arrays entry to index into; no bounds check was performed against the actual array size, so a crafted value produces an out-of-bounds read off the end of the static global array. Fix introduces N_SCIDX_* macros for each array's size and adds bounds checks before indexing.

Heap-use-after-free READ (1 byte) in cff_blend_doBlend() (src/cff/cffload.c), reached via cff_parser_run -> cff_load_private_dict while parsing a CFF Private DICT with two or more consecutive `blend` operators. Each blend op may need to grow subFont->blend_stack via FT_REALLOC; when realloc moves the buffer, blend_top is correctly reset, but parser->stack entries from a *previous* blend op in the same DICT still point into the old (now-freed) allocation. A second blend op in a row reads through one of those stale parser->stack pointers, hitting freed heap memory. Fix adjusts every parser->stack pointer that fell inside the old buffer by the realloc's address delta.
